BiblicalUsage: Zarephath was a town of Sidon, between Tyre and Sidon on the sea coast. The LORD sent Elijah there in the famine, to a widow whose meal and oil did not fail while the drought lasted; and Obadiah says the captives of Israel will possess the land as far as Zarephath. A Gentile town became the scene of one of the greatest miracles of provision.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God feeds His people in the unlikeliest places — a widow in a Gentile town, in a famine, with a handful of meal. Zarephath is proof that His provision is not bound by borders.
